en.title: SPACE
en.desc: Selected professional architecture work focused on the decisions behind form: solar access, public realm, street scale, façade expression, views and environmental performance.
en.question: How can architectural form respond to yield and technical constraints without losing spatial quality, identity and human scale?
en.built: The project brings together three professional studies. 60 Denmark Street is presented as the main case study, using massing, solar analysis, physical modelling and public-realm design. Iglu Arden and 87 Queensbridge extend the same design thinking into façade systems and high-rise form.
en.judgement: I am most interested in design moves that have visible consequences. A change in orientation, proportion or geometry should improve something tangible — daylight, views, public space, efficiency or the experience of the street — rather than exist as form for its own sake.
taste: KEEP
Design moves with measurable spatial consequences: better light, views, public realm or efficiency.
REMOVE
Formal complexity that cannot explain what it improves.
TEST
Bring computational feedback earlier into massing so performance and architectural judgement evolve together.

zh.title: SPACE
zh.brief: 建筑设计 / 专业项目精选
zh.meta: 总体规划 / 可行性研究 / 竞赛 / 计算分析
zh.role: 设计 / 计算分析 / 视觉表达
zh.output: 建筑设计 / 投标 + 竞赛方案
zh.desc: 精选专业建筑项目，重点不是最终造型本身，而是造型背后的判断：日照、公共空间、街道尺度、立面表达、景观视野与环境性能。
zh.question: 建筑形式如何在产出与技术约束之间取得平衡，同时保留空间品质、识别性与人的尺度？
zh.built: 该项目整合三个专业案例。60 Denmark Street 作为主案例，通过体量、日照分析、实体模型与公共空间设计展开；Iglu Arden 与 87 Queensbridge 则将相同的设计思维延伸到立面系统和高层建筑形体。
zh.judgement: 我更关注会产生清晰后果的设计动作。朝向、比例或几何的变化应该真正改善日照、视野、公共空间、效率或街道体验，而不是为了形式本身而增加复杂度。
taste: 保留
能够带来可衡量空间结果的设计动作：更好的日照、视野、公共空间或效率。
移除
无法说明其具体价值的形式复杂度。
测试
让计算反馈更早进入体量设计，使性能判断与建筑判断同步演化。

en.title: SYSTEM
en.role: SYSTEM DESIGN / INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE / UX / PROTOTYPING
en.tools: HTML / CSS / JS / MAPBOX / RHINO / GRASSHOPPER
en.desc: A body of work about making complex design information usable — from studio knowledge and recurring resources to spatial city data and browser-based interfaces.
en.question: How can complex information become easier to navigate without flattening the structure, context and relationships that make it useful?
en.built: Selected systems include Studio Library, which reframes fragmented internal resources around designer intent, and city-data workflows that connect spatial models, urban information and web interfaces. The portfolio presents Studio Library as the main interactive case study.
en.judgement: The recurring decision is what not to expose. I reduce internal structure, technical noise and repeated information so the interface can surface the right context at the moment it becomes useful.
taste: KEEP
Clear entry points that match the way a designer actually searches, asks and navigates.
REMOVE
Internal structure, tool taxonomy and data density that force the user to understand the system before using it.
TEST
How search, spatial browsing and progressive disclosure can shorten the distance between a question and a useful answer.

zh.title: SYSTEM
zh.brief: 信息 + 城市数据 / 知识系统
zh.meta: 信息架构 / 城市数据 / 前端
zh.role: 系统设计 / 信息架构 / UX / 原型开发
zh.tools: HTML / CSS / JS / MAPBOX / RHINO / GRASSHOPPER
zh.output: 交互式信息 + 知识系统
zh.desc: 一组关于“如何让复杂设计信息真正可用”的工作：从事务所知识与高频资源，到城市空间数据与浏览器界面。
zh.question: 怎样让复杂信息更容易被导航，同时又不抹平真正有价值的结构、上下文与关系？
zh.built: 这一部分包括 Studio Library，以及把空间模型、城市数据与网页界面连接起来的城市数据工作流。作品集以 Studio Library 作为主要可交互案例。
zh.judgement: 反复出现的判断是：什么不应该直接暴露给用户。我会减少内部结构、技术噪音与重复信息，让真正有用的上下文在需要的时候出现。
taste: 保留
符合设计师真实搜索、提问与导航方式的清晰入口。
移除
要求用户先理解系统才能使用的内部结构、工具分类与过量数据。
测试
搜索、空间浏览与渐进式信息展示，能否缩短从问题到有效答案的距离。

en.title: CODE
en.tools: RHINO / GRASSHOPPER / PYTHON / HTML / CSS / JS / AI AGENTS
en.desc: A collection of computational tools and prototypes built to reduce friction between design intent and execution — across Rhino workflows, automation, scripting and browser-based interaction.
en.question: When does code become useful to a designer? The work focuses on places where computation removes repetition, exposes choices or makes an idea easier to test.
en.built: The body of work includes Rhino Tabs and studio tooling, Grasshopper and Python workflows, and rapid web prototypes built with coding agents. The common thread is not a specific language or platform, but the translation of recurring design problems into usable systems.
en.judgement: The tool should disappear behind the task. I remove technical complexity, generic AI effects and unnecessary features until the useful action is obvious and the interaction feels intentional.
taste: KEEP
Tools that make a recurring design action faster, clearer or easier to test.
REMOVE
Technical complexity and generated effects that do not improve the task.
TEST
How far a prototype can be simplified before it loses the capability that made it useful.

zh.title: CODE
zh.brief: 计算设计 / 自动化 / 交互工具
zh.role: 计算设计 / 工具开发 / 原型
zh.tools: RHINO / GRASSHOPPER / PYTHON / HTML / CSS / JS / AI AGENTS
zh.output: 设计工具 / 自动化 / 交互原型
zh.desc: 一组为了减少“设计意图”和“实际执行”之间摩擦而搭建的计算工具与原型，覆盖 Rhino 工作流、自动化、脚本与浏览器交互。
zh.question: 代码什么时候才真正对设计师有用？这一部分关注的是那些计算可以减少重复、暴露选择，或让想法更容易被测试的节点。
zh.built: 内容包括 Rhino Tabs 与事务所工具、Grasshopper / Python 工作流，以及通过 coding agents 快速搭建的网页原型。它们的共同点不是某一种语言，而是把反复出现的设计问题转译成可使用的系统。
zh.judgement: 工具应该退到任务之后。我会删掉技术复杂度、通用的 AI 特效与多余功能，直到真正有用的动作足够清楚，交互也足够有意图。
media: AI 原型 / WEB 交互
taste: 保留
让高频设计动作更快、更清楚或更容易测试的工具。
移除
不能改善任务本身的技术复杂度与生成式特效。
测试
原型可以被简化到什么程度，而不失去真正有价值的能力。

en.title: OBSERVATION
en.desc: Photography as an ongoing exercise in attention: people, buildings, incidental gestures and landscape fragments selected over the years, mostly in medium and 135 format film, with a small amount of digital work as supplement.
en.question: What makes an image worth keeping when nothing dramatic is happening? The section treats selection and sequencing as a way to make visual judgement explicit.
en.built: An evolving body of street, architectural, landscape and observational photography. The work moves slowly through contact sheets and sequences, and the edit is treated as part of the image-making.
en.judgement: I look for tension between geometry and behaviour, clarity without over-composition, and frames that gain more meaning when they sit beside another frame. The edit matters as much as the shutter.
taste: KEEP
Images with one clear visual reason to exist, even when the subject is ordinary.
REMOVE
Technically clean photographs that say the same thing as a stronger frame.
TEST
Whether a sequence produces a new reading that no single image can carry alone.

zh.title: OBSERVATION
zh.brief: 摄影 / 年份 / 碎片
zh.meta: 中画幅 / 135 胶片 / 数码补充
zh.tools: 相机 / 序列 / 编辑
zh.desc: 把摄影当作一种持续的注意力练习：人物、建筑、偶然动作与风景碎片，跨越不同年份拍摄，主要以中画幅与 135 胶片为主，少量数码作为补充。
zh.question: 当没有明显戏剧事件发生时，什么样的图像仍然值得被保留？这个部分把“挑选”与“排序”当成显化视觉判断的方法。
zh.built: 一个持续生长的街头、建筑、风景与观察性影像集合。作品通过接触表和序列慢慢成形，编辑本身被视为拍摄的一部分。
zh.judgement: 我在意几何与行为之间的张力、清晰但不过度构图的画面，以及一张图像与另一张图像并置后产生的新含义。快门和编辑同样重要。
media: 序列 / 编辑 / 节奏
taste: 保留
即使主题平常，也有明确视觉理由存在的图像。
去除
技术上很干净、但表达重复于更强画面的照片。
测试
一个序列是否能产生单张图像无法承担的新阅读。

en.title: RESEARCH
en.meta: URBAN DATA / MACHINE LEARNING / PLANNING TOOL
en.tools: PYTHON / MACHINE LEARNING / URBAN DATA / VISUALISATION
en.desc: My graduation thesis explored TODAI, a machine-learning-powered planning tool for Transit-Oriented Development, bringing urban data, computational analysis and planning decisions into one research workflow.
en.question: Can a planning tool use data and machine learning to support early-stage urban design decisions while keeping the designer inside the decision-making loop?
en.built: The research connects planning inputs, computational analysis and model outputs into a tool-oriented workflow. This section will present the thesis as a visual research artifact rather than reproducing the original academic paper page by page.
en.judgement: The important distinction is between prediction and decision. The model can surface patterns and alternatives, but the value of the tool depends on how those outputs are framed, compared and interpreted by a designer.
taste: KEEP
Research steps that make the relationship between input, model and design decision legible.
REMOVE
Academic detail that does not help explain how the system works or why the result matters.
TEST
How the original research can be reframed as an interactive explanation rather than a static thesis document.

zh.title: RESEARCH
zh.brief: TODAI / 机器学习 + 公共交通导向开发
zh.meta: 城市数据 / 机器学习 / 规划工具
zh.role: 研究 / 计算设计 / 界面
zh.tools: PYTHON / 机器学习 / 城市数据 / 可视化
zh.output: 毕业论文 / 规划原型
zh.desc: 我的毕业论文研究 TODAI——一个由机器学习驱动的 Transit-Oriented Development 规划工具，把城市数据、计算分析与规划判断整合进同一套研究工作流。
zh.question: 规划工具能否利用数据与机器学习辅助早期城市设计，同时仍然让设计师保留在真正的决策环节中？
zh.built: 研究把规划输入、计算分析与模型输出连接成工具化工作流。这个章节会把论文重新组织成一个视觉化 research artifact，而不是逐页复制原始学术论文。
zh.judgement: 关键区别在于“预测”和“决策”并不是一回事。模型可以暴露模式与备选方案，但工具真正的价值取决于这些结果如何被组织、比较，并由设计师解释。
media: 界面 / 输出 / 评估
taste: 保留
能够清楚说明输入、模型与设计决策之间关系的研究步骤。
移除
不能帮助理解系统如何工作或结果为何重要的学术细节。
测试
如何把原始论文重新组织成可交互的解释，而不是静态论文页面。
